name: Romania
summary: Possession for own use is a crime (Law 143/2000): 'risk' drugs incl. cannabis, ketamine, GHB, benzos: 3 months–2 yrs or fine; 'high-risk' drugs: 6 months–3 yrs or fine. First offences are often waived or deferred.

poisonControl.name: Toxicological Information Office, National Institute of Public Health (INSP), weekday office hours

callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Medical staff are bound by confidentiality, but police can become involved in drug cases and possession of any amount is a crime.
drugChecking: No established public drug checking service is known in Romania.

wikiCannabis.title: Wikipedia: Cannabis in Romania (illegal; 2013 low-THC medical law; 2023 '3 grame' bill rejected)

wikiLegality.title: Wikipedia: Legality of cannabis (Romania: small quantities – fine for first offenders)

wikiMush.title: Wikipedia: Legal status of psilocybin mushrooms (Romania: illegal)

wikiAyahuasca.title: Wikipedia: Legal status of ayahuasca by country (Romania: illegal)

un1971.title: INCB Green List: psychotropic substances under international control (1971 Convention)

euN2O.title: EU Perspectives (Mar 2026): nitrous oxide classified reprotoxic; large canisters may be barred from consumer sale from Feb 2027

l143.title: Law 143/2000 on drug trafficking and consumption: art. 1 (risk vs high-risk), art. 4, annex tables I–IV (unofficial consolidated text; penalties revised in 2014)

l143anexa.title: Law 143/2000 annex: drug tables I–III (unofficial consolidated text)

lsd.note: Table I high-risk drug: possession for own use 6 months–3 yrs or a fine; first offences are often waived or deferred.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin, psilocin and all Psilocybe species are Table I high-risk drugs; possessing or growing them is a crime.

dmt.note: Table I high-risk drug; possession is a crime. Ayahuasca possession, sale and cultivation are illegal.

mescaline.note: Table I high-risk drug; possession is a crime (6 months–3 yrs or a fine).

dox.note: DOB, DOC, DOI, DOET are Table I high-risk drugs; possession is a crime.

nbomes.note: 25I/25B/25C-NBOMe are UN Schedule I and nationally controlled; possession is a crime.

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other 2C-x are UN-scheduled and controlled as high-risk drugs; possession is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are Table I high-risk drugs; possession is a crime.

5-meo-xxt.note: Not UN-scheduled; whether 5-MeO tryptamines are on Romania's drug tables or only covered by the NPS law was not verified.

cannabis.note: Table III 'risk' drug: possession for own use 3 months–2 yrs or a fine; first offenders often get a waiver. Only low-THC medicines allowed, none marketed.

ketamine.note: Table III 'risk' drug and a prescription/veterinary anaesthetic: possession without a prescription is a crime (3 months–2 yrs or fine).

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is UN Schedule II; possession is a crime.

dxm.note: Not internationally controlled; pharmacy (OTC vs prescription) status in Romania was not verified.

nitrous.note: Restrictions on recreational sale have been debated; the current national rules were not verified. EU limits on large canisters may apply from 2027.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are Table II high-risk drugs: possession for own use is a crime. ADHD stimulants are strictly controlled.

mdma.note: Table I high-risk drug: possession for own use 6 months–3 yrs or a fine; first offences are often waived or deferred.

cocaine.note: Table II high-risk drug: possession for own use 6 months–3 yrs or a fine.

caffeine.note: Legal and not a controlled substance.

alcohol.note: Legal from 18; sale to minors is prohibited.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is a Table III 'risk' drug: possession is a crime (3 months–2 yrs or fine). Status of GBL/1,4-BD not verified.

opioids.note: Heroin (Table I) and fentanyl, morphine etc. (Tables I–II) are high-risk: possession 6 months–3 yrs or fine. Medical opioids need a prescription.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine; not found in the drug tables, so possession without a prescription is likely not a drug crime.

benzodiazepines.note: Diazepam and other benzodiazepines are Table III 'risk' drugs: possession without a prescription is a crime (3 months–2 yrs or fine).

maois.note: Pharmaceutical MAOIs are prescription-only. Status of harmala/Syrian rue not verified; ayahuasca (DMT) is illegal.
